title: Opinions & discussions
goal: Hold your own in a discussion: give your view, agree and disagree without starting a fight, say 'it depends', 'maybe' and 'must be', argue about cricket, and say what someone should have done.
intro:
Gujaratis love a good discussion — about cricket, prices, traffic, politics, which **ખમણ** shop is best — at the tea stall, on the family WhatsApp group, over dinner. This unit gives you the tools to join in: ways to give your view (**મારા હિસાબે…**, **સાચું કહું તો…**), to disagree without offending (**વાત તો સાચી, પણ…**), to hedge (**કદાચ**, **હોઈ શકે**, **હશે**), and to say what should have happened (**બૉલિંગ લેવી જોઈતી હતી!**).

There's also a full set of cricket words, because sooner or later someone will turn on the match.

grammar.title: Maybe, might, must be: કદાચ, હોઈ શકે, હશે
grammar.body:
Gujarati has three handy ways to say how sure you are.

**1. કદાચ 'maybe'** — with the **subjunctive** (less sure) or the **future** (more likely):
**કદાચ** એ મોડો **આવે** 'he might be late'
**કદાચ** વરસાદ **પડશે** 'it'll probably rain'

**2. -ઈ શકે 'could, might'** — the verb **શકવું** 'can' (unit 15) also means 'it's possible':
આ વખતે ગુજરાત **જીતી શકે છે** 'Gujarat could win this time'
**હોઈ શકે** 'could be, maybe' — on its own as an answer, or with **કે** + subjunctive: **હોઈ શકે કે** મેં ખોટું સાંભળ્યું **હોય** 'it could be that I heard wrong'.

**3. હશે 'must be, probably is'** — the future of હોવું is used for a confident guess about **now**:
એ ટ્રાફિકમાં **હશે** 'he must be in traffic'
અત્યારે ત્યાં રાત **હશે** 'it must be night-time there now'
With a past form it's a guess about the **past**: એ નીકળી ગયો **હશે** 'he must have left', ફોન ગાડીમાં રહી ગયો **હશે** 'the phone must have been left in the car'. The past form agrees as usual (ગયો / ગઈ / ગયું / ગયા).

**The trap:** **હશે** doesn't only mean 'will be'. એ ઘરે **હશે** is usually 'he'll be at home (I expect)', a guess about right now — to say 'he will be at home tomorrow' you need the time word: કાલે એ ઘરે **હશે**.

examples.en: He must be stuck in traffic.

grammar.title: Disagreeing politely and 'I don't think…'
grammar.body:
**'I don't think…'** In Gujarati, as in English, the 'not' goes on 'think': **મને નથી લાગતું કે** + the clause, with the **future** for things to come: **મને નથી લાગતું કે** એ આવશે 'I don't think he'll come'. Also **મને એવું નથી લાગતું** 'I don't think so' (unit 14).

**Giving your view:** **મારા હિસાબે…** 'the way I see it', **મને લાગે છે કે…**, **સાચું કહું તો…** 'to be honest', and to ask: **તને શું લાગે છે?** (friend) or **તમારું શું માનવું છે?** (polite).

**Disagreeing, from soft to firm:**
**વાત તો સાચી, પણ…** 'true, but…' — accept part of it first
**તારો મુદ્દો સમજું છું, પણ…** 'I get your point, but…'
**હું સહમત નથી / હું અસહમત છું** 'I don't agree'
**એવું નથી** 'that's not how it is', **વાત ઊંધી છે** 'it's the other way round'
**બિલકુલ નહીં!** 'absolutely not!'

**It depends:** **એ … પર આધાર રાખે છે** (careful), **એ તો ડિપેન્ડ કરે છે** (everyday). **શું ફરક પડે છે?** 'what difference does it make?'

**Cooling things down:** **ચાલ, આમાં ઝઘડવાનું નથી**, **જવા દે** 'let it go'.

**The trap:** with elders, a flat **એવું નથી** or **તમે ખોટા છો** sounds rude. Use the soft openers, **તમે** and a question: **પણ એવું ન હોય?** 'but couldn't it be that…?'

grammar.title: Should have, could have: -વું જોઈતું હતું, -ઈ શક્યા હોત
grammar.body:
**Should have** is the past of **-વું જોઈએ** 'should' (unit 9): **-વું જોઈતું હતું**. The person takes the **-એ form** (મારે, તારે, એણે, આપણે, તમારે…), as with all obligation:

**તારે** મને **કહેવું જોઈતું હતું** 'you should have told me'
**આપણે** વહેલા **નીકળવું જોઈતું હતું** 'we should have left earlier'

As always, the infinitive **and** જોઈતું હતું agree with the **object** (unit 25):
બૉલિંગ (f) **લેવી જોઈતી હતી** · ફોન (m) **કરવો જોઈતો હતો** · કામ (n) **કરવું જોઈતું હતું**

**Shouldn't have:** put **નહોતું** (agreeing) in: મારે એટલું તીખું **નહોતું** ખાવું **જોઈતું** 'I shouldn't have eaten something so spicy'; મારે એ વાત **નહોતી** કહેવી જોઈતી.

**Could have** uses **શકવું** + **હોત** (the 'would have' form from unit 19): આપણે મૅચ **જીતી શક્યા હોત** 'we could have won the match'. Often with an if-clause: થોડી વધારે મહેનત કરી **હોત તો** જીતી **શક્યા હોત**.

**Didn't need to:** **-વાની જરૂર નહોતી**: એણે છગ્ગો મારવાની **જરૂર નહોતી** 'he didn't need to go for a six'.

**The trap:** don't use the plain past for 'should have': 'he should have bowled first' is એણે પહેલાં બૉલિંગ **લેવી જોઈતી હતી**, not 'લીધી'. And the person is **તારે / એણે**, never 'તું / એ'.

culture: Opinions flow freely in Gujarat, especially among friends of the same age — at the **ચાની કીટલી** (tea stall) or the **પાનનો ગલ્લો**, where men have been settling politics, cricket and the price of petrol for generations. Ahmedabad is home to the Narendra Modi Stadium, the biggest cricket ground in the world, and Gujarat Titans' IPL games fill it; during a big India match whole offices go quiet. Prices (**મોંઘવારી**), traffic and the weather are safe topics with anyone. Politics and religion are best left alone with people you don't know well, and with elders you disagree softly: **તમારી વાત બરાબર, પણ…**, with **તમે**, and never a flat **તમે ખોટા છો**. Between friends, heated arguments are part of the fun and end with **ચાલ, જવા દે** and another cup of tea. In the diaspora, the same arguments happen on family WhatsApp groups — usually in a mix of Gujarati and English.

tip.title: Saying what you think
tip.body:
- Give your view with **મારા હિસાબે…**, **મને લાગે છે કે…** or **સાચું કહું તો…** 'to be honest'.
- Ask a friend **તને શું લાગે છે?**; politely: **તમારું શું માનવું છે?**
- Accept part of a point first: **વાત તો સાચી, પણ…**

lessons.title: Disagreeing without a fight

tip.title: I don't think… and polite no's
tip.body:
- 'I don't think…' = **મને નથી લાગતું કે** + future: મને નથી લાગતું કે એ **આવશે**.
- Soft: **તારો મુદ્દો સમજું છું, પણ…** · firm: **એવું નથી**, **હું સહમત નથી** · strongest: **બિલકુલ નહીં!**
- Cool it down: **ચાલ, આમાં ઝઘડવાનું નથી**.
- With elders, stay soft and use **તમે**.

sentences.roman: yār, dalīl na kar, bas mānī jā.
sentences.en: Mate, don't argue, just accept it.

tip.title: How sure are you?
tip.body:
- **કદાચ** + subjunctive or future: કદાચ એ **આવે** / **આવશે**.
- **-ઈ શકે**, **હોઈ શકે** 'could, might': એ સાચો **હોઈ શકે**.
- **હશે** 'must be' (a guess about now): એ ઘરે **હશે**; past: એ નીકળી ગયો **હશે** 'he must have left'.

sentences.en: He must be stuck in traffic.
The match might be cancelled today.
Gujarat have a chance this time.
He could be right, too.
They must have left.

sentences.native: મારો ફોન ક્યાં છે? કદાચ ગાડીમાં રહી ગયો હશે.
sentences.roman: māro fon kyāṃ chhe? kadāch gāḍīmāṃ rahī gayo hashe.
sentences.en: Where's my phone? I must have left it in the car.
The chances of winning are slim.
It's going to be really hot tomorrow.

sentences.native: એ તો હવામાન પર આધાર રાખે છે.
sentences.roman: e to havāmān par ādhār rākhe chhe.
sentences.en: That depends on the weather.
What difference will that make?

tip.title: Cricket talk
tip.body:
- Cricket talk is half English: **બૅટિંગ, બૉલિંગ, ટૉસ, આઉટ, સ્કોર**.
- Winning takes the ergative and agrees with what's won: ઇન્ડિયા**એ** ટૉસ **જીત્યો** (m), મૅચ **જીતી** (f).
- A six is a **છગ્ગો**, a four a **ચોગ્ગો**: છગ્ગો **માર્યો** 'hit a six'.

sentences.en: India won the toss.
India chose to bat first.
Wow, what a six!
He hit three fours in a row.

sentences.native: આપણી બૉલિંગ આજે બહુ ખરાબ હતી.
sentences.roman: āpaṇī boliṅg āje bahu kharāb hatī.
sentences.en: Our bowling was awful today.
Kohli's out!
Which team's winning?
What's the score?

sentences.native: ચાલ, મૅચ જોવા મારા ઘરે આવ!
sentences.roman: chāl, mech jovā mārā ghare āv!
sentences.en: Come over to mine to watch the match!
The stadium was packed.

tip.title: Should have, could have
tip.body:
- 'Should have' = **-વું જોઈતું હતું**, doer in the -એ form: **તારે** કહેવું **જોઈતું હતું**.
- It agrees with the object: બૉલિંગ (f) **લેવી જોઈતી હતી**, ફોન (m) **કરવો જોઈતો હતો**.
- 'Shouldn't have': add **નહોતું** (agreeing).
- 'Could have' = **-ઈ શક્યા હોત**: જીતી **શક્યા હોત**.

sentences.native: આપણે ટૉસ જીતીને બૉલિંગ લેવી જોઈતી હતી.
sentences.roman: āpaṇe ṭos jītīne boliṅg levī joītī hatī.
sentences.en: We should have bowled after winning the toss.

sentences.native: તારે મને પહેલાં ફોન કરવો જોઈતો હતો.
sentences.roman: tāre mane pahelāṃ fon karvo joīto hato.
sentences.en: You should have called me first.

sentences.native: અમ્પાયરે વધારે ધ્યાન આપવું જોઈતું હતું.
sentences.roman: ampāyare vadhāre dhyān āpvuṃ joītuṃ hatuṃ.
sentences.en: The umpire should have paid more attention.

sentences.native: થોડી વધારે મહેનત કરી હોત તો આપણે જીતી શક્યા હોત.
sentences.roman: thoḍī vadhāre mahenat karī hot to āpaṇe jītī shakyā hot.
sentences.en: With a bit more effort we could have won.

sentences.native: મારે એ વાત નહોતી કહેવી જોઈતી.
sentences.roman: māre e vāt nahotī kahevī joītī.
sentences.en: I shouldn't have said that.

sentences.native: એ આઉટ નહોતો, અમ્પાયર ખોટો હતો!
sentences.roman: e āuṭ nahoto, ampāyar khoṭo hato!
sentences.en: He wasn't out, the umpire got it wrong!
He didn't need to go for a six.

sentences.native: તું સાચો હતો, મારે તારું માનવું જોઈતું હતું.
sentences.roman: tuṃ sācho hato, māre tāruṃ mānvuṃ joītuṃ hatuṃ.
sentences.en: You were right, I should have listened to you.

sentences.native: અમે વહેલા નીકળ્યા હોત તો મૅચ શરૂથી જોઈ શક્યા હોત.
sentences.roman: ame vahelā nīkaḷyā hot to mech sharūthī joī shakyā hot.
sentences.en: If we'd left earlier we could have watched the match from the start.
He was clearly out.

tip.title: Everyday big topics
tip.body:
- Prices, traffic and pollution are safe small talk with anyone: **મોંઘવારી બહુ વધી ગઈ છે**.
- Politics is best kept for friends; with elders, hedge with **મારા હિસાબે** and **કદાચ**.
- Change the subject: **ચાલ, રાજકારણની વાત બંધ કરીએ**.

sentences.native: આજકાલ મોંઘવારી બહુ વધી ગઈ છે.
sentences.roman: ājkāl moṃghvārī bahu vadhī gaī chhe.
sentences.en: Prices have shot up these days.
I don't like talking politics.

sentences.native: બધા નેતા એક જેવા જ છે.
sentences.roman: badhā netā ek jevā j chhe.
sentences.en: Politicians are all the same.
The government has built a new bridge.
The government might change.

sentences.native: મારા હિસાબે ટ્રાફિક સૌથી મોટો મુદ્દો છે.
sentences.roman: mārā hisābe ṭrāfik sauthī moṭo muddo chhe.
sentences.en: In my view traffic is the biggest issue.
When's the election?
Pollution gets worse in winter.
Are you going to vote this time?
Come on, let's stop talking politics.
